newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Cyprus protests to U.N. at killing of Greek Cypriot.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus protests to U.N. at killing of Greek Cypriot.

text.p: Cyprus protested to the United Nations on Wednesday over the killing of a Greek Cypriot who entered Turkish Cypriot-controlled territory last Sunday and called for steps to end such "criminal acts."

In a letter to Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, Cypriot U.N. representative Nicos Agathocleous said this was "the fourth cold-blooded killing of unarmed Greek Cypriots over the past three months" and that "in all instances, no danger whatsoever was posed to the Turkish occupation forces."
The island has been virtually partitioned since 1974 when Turkish troops landed in northern Cyprus in response to a Greek-engineered coup in Nicosia.
Agathocleous said Turkish allegations that soldiers "fired warning shots and then shot the victim while he was trying to escape" were disproved by eyewitness testimony.

Referring to the recent fatal incidents, he said the "sinister objective of these Turkish criminal actions is to further the division and partition of the island and promote the Turkish position that it is supposedly impossible for the two communities to live together in a reunited Cyprus."

He strongly protested the "brutal crime committed yet again by the Turkish occupation forces in Cyprus" and called on the secretary-general and the Security Council to "take all necessary steps to end these criminal acts" and to see that those responsible were held fully accountable and brought to justice.

The president of the Security Council, in a statement read to reporters Tuesday, said the council deeply regretted Sunday's incident and "condemns in the strongest terms this unjustified act that only contributes to increased tensions in the island."
A Turkish Cypriot soldier was also killed in a shooting incident last month.
